reason: The text introduces Job as the primary character—a regular man from the land of Uz with a family, possessions, and servants. Job is explicitly portrayed with emotions (grief expressed through tearing his garments, shaving his head, and falling to the ground) and has multiple lines of dialogue expressing his beliefs ('Naked came I out of my mother's womb...', 'The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD'). Additionally, the passage features multiple unnamed messengers/servants who arrive with lines of dialogue ('I alone escaped alone to tell thee') and convey emotional responses to disaster. Even secondary characters like Job's sons and daughters are depicted as social beings engaged in feasting together. While the text also includes divine characters (God and Satan), the core narrative centers on Job as a regular human character with emotions, opinions, and agency.
